name: Bazaar Balancer-fork exitPool without sender validation
summary: The Bazaar vault, a Balancer fork, passed exitPool's caller-chosen sender to the LBP without checking that the caller was that sender or its approved relayer, and the LBP only required sender to be its owner. The attacker exited the only registered LBP naming its owner as sender and itself as recipient, taking the pool's WETH and rYOLO.
notes: Non-upgradeable vault; registerPool is permissionless, so the LBP's registration is a user action, not a reset. The vault holds a single pool (poolNonce 1), and the team's own later exit of the remainder (0xe75637e3, sent by the vault deployer) is an affiliated rescue.

The self-described whitehat returned 353.13 of the 392.37 ETH about two hours later, after an onchain bounty offer from the team, and never returned the rYOLO. That makes it a negotiated return of a theft, not an affiliated rescue (rule 5), and recoveries are not subtracted (rule 11).
rYOLO has no DefiLlama price and the attacker never sold it, so it is valued at zero realised proceeds; the total is a floor.
